title: The Dharma-Gate of the Ground of Mind
author: Annotated by Zhanran
excerpt: Ordinary beings and sages do not go beyond the one mind; good and evil are both created by the mind.

inline.s: Recorded Teachings of Dharma Master Huiming
Ordinary beings and sages do not go beyond the one mind; good and evil are both created by the mind.
Destiny is established by oneself; fortune is sought by oneself.
Good deeds and hidden merits are all created by the mind; if one constantly preserves this mind, one's merit and virtue are immeasurable.
Do no evil, practice all good, purify one's own mind — this is the teaching of all Buddhas.
[This is the teaching of all Buddhas] This is what all the Buddhas teach.

[The good and evil of people all arise from the mind. When the mind is good, one is a Buddha; when the mind is evil, one is a demon. Buddha and demon have no fixed nature; they merely shift according to the good or evil of one's thoughts.]

The good and evil of people all arise from the mind. When the mind is good, one is a Buddha; when the mind is evil, one is a demon. Being a Buddha or a demon has no fixed nature; one merely shifts according to the good or evil of one's thoughts.

[Honesty, humility, compassion, diligence, and frugality are good thoughts; deceit, arrogance, hatred, lust, and indolence are evil thoughts. Therefore, with a single good thought, the Buddha responds, and body, mind, and surroundings become harmonious and are transformed toward the Buddha. Not only do the good become better, but the evil are also turned toward good. With a single evil thought, the demon responds, and body, mind, and surroundings turn harsh and are transformed toward the demon; not only do the evil become worse, but the good are also turned toward evil. Hence it is said: 'Ordinary beings and sages do not go beyond the one mind; good and evil are both created by the mind.' When the mind is Buddha, one is Buddha; when the mind is demon, one is demon. This is the natural principle.]

Honesty, humility, compassion, diligence, and frugality are good thoughts; deceit, arrogance, hatred, lust, and indolence are evil thoughts. Therefore, with a single good thought, the Buddha responds, and body, mind, and surroundings become harmonious and are transformed toward the Buddha. Not only do the good become better, but the evil are also turned toward good. With a single evil thought, the demon responds, and body, mind, and surroundings turn harsh and are transformed toward the demon; not only do the evil become worse, but the good are also turned toward evil. Hence it is said: 'Ordinary beings and sages do not go beyond the one mind; good and evil are both created by the mind.' When the mind acts as Buddha, one is Buddha; when the mind acts as demon, one is demon. This is only natural.

[In the age of the Dharma's decline, people are mostly deluded and benighted, unclear about good and evil, and so entrap themselves in affliction. There are even those who harbor a treacherous, devious heart yet deliberately speak good words, thinking that all people can be deceived and that none in the world is wiser than they. Little do they know that the vicious evil demons have already gathered in their bodies and minds. Once their karma is set in motion, at the least they meet with sickness, suffering, and ruin, and at the worst they sink into the evil destinies. Even if, relying on past good causes, they escape for a time, once their blessings are exhausted, the evil retribution is endless — is this not perilous? This principle that 'doing good brings down good fortune and doing evil brings down calamity' has never erred through all the ages.]

In the age of the Dharma's decline, people are mostly deluded and benighted, unclear about good and evil, and so entrap themselves in affliction. There are even those who harbor a treacherous, devious heart (crafty and cunning), yet deliberately speak good words, thinking that everyone in the world can be deceived and that none of them is wiser than themselves. Little do they know that the vicious evil demons have already gathered in their bodies and minds. Once their karma is set in motion, at the least they meet with sickness, suffering, and ruin, and at the worst they sink into the evil destinies. Even if, relying on past good causes, they escape for a time, once their blessings are exhausted, the evil retribution is endless — is this not perilous? This principle that 'doing good brings down good fortune and doing evil brings down calamity' has passed through all ages without the slightest error!

[In short, Buddha and demon are not apart from one's own mind. Why? Because everything is mind-only. As it is said, when the mind arises, all dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease. But dharmas have no self-nature, no deviance or rectitude. If the mind is upright, even a deviant practice becomes upright; if the mind is deviant, even an upright practice becomes deviant. When the mind is good, the demon is transformed into a Buddha; when the mind is evil, the Buddha is transformed into a demon. At the moment we raise a thought, can we afford not to be careful?]

In short, being Buddha or demon is not apart from one's own mind. Why? Because everything is mind-only. As it is said, 'when the mind arises, all dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease.' However, dharmas have no self-nature, no deviance or rectitude. If the mind is upright, even a deviant practice becomes upright; if the mind is deviant, even an upright practice becomes deviant. When the mind is good, the demon is transformed into a Buddha; when the mind is evil, the Buddha is transformed into a demon. When we raise a thought, can we afford not to be extremely careful?
From this we know that 'transforming baleful energy into harmony, and turning calamity and early death into fortune and longevity' lies precisely at the moment of raising a thought.
